answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared harbor registry before it may trade. Newcomers start with a small walnut-sized bond that only grows as they complete verified work, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real capital per identity. Peers mirror each other's behavior records on a public ledger, so a Sybil cluster rating itself highly leaves an obvious mirrored pattern, and proven fraud burns the whole stake.
